message.content: The obvious risk: when a row's mask keeps nothing, `x - tl.max(x)` becomes `-inf - (-inf) = NaN`, and dividing 0/0 gives NaN instead of the contractually required all-zero row. I'll record this claim and run a probe.

message.reasoning_content:
Key risk: empty mask row. If keep all False: x = -inf everywhere, x - max = -inf - (-inf) = NaN... actually -inf - (-inf) = nan. e = where(keep, exp(nan), 0) = 0 (keep false). sum = 0 → 0/0 = NaN → NaN output. So empty rows produce NaN, violating "all-zero output row" and "every returned value must be finite". This is explicitly in the contract, in_scope.

Record claim and probe.
